mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by 2% or more year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 5.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of 1% or more for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by 1% or more for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by 1% or more for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and accelerating inflation, increasing uncertainty and risk premia, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between housing starts (HOUST) and personal savings (RSAFS) over the past six months indicates robust household balance sheets and housing demand, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: Pearson correlation(HOUST, RSAFS) > 0.6 over last 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST and RSAFS are strongly positively correlated over the prior six months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of at least 50,000 for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, supporting consumer demand and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 50,000 for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS rises by at least 50,000 for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average, combined with a concurrent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals deteriorating household finances and reduced consumption, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month moving average AND UNRATE rising
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is below its 12-month moving average and UNRATE is rising concurrently.
